Spending time in the Conservatory Garden gives you a deeper appreciation for how much history and labor sit behind every corner of @centralparknyc. This space didn’t just appear — it evolved from a 19th-century nursery into the formal garden we know today, shaped by decades of redesign, restoration, and continuous upkeep.

What stands out now is how intentionally the Garden has been renewed. The recent multi-year restoration wasn’t just cosmetic — it strengthened the infrastructure, improved accessibility, and ensured the Garden could support heavy foot traffic while still protecting its plant collections. Walking through the North, Center, and South Gardens, you can feel how much thought went into preserving their character while bringing them into a healthier future.

It’s a reminder that public gardens only thrive when people invest in them — planners, horticulturists, historians, volunteers, and everyday visitors who value the role green spaces play in city life. The Conservatory Garden is a living record of that shared commitment, and I’m grateful to everyone at @centralparknyc who works to keep it flourishing.

Standing in the Conservatory Garden, it’s easy to get swept up in the beauty — but the real story starts months before anything blooms. The work happening in @centralparknyc right now is thoughtful, strategic, and rooted in deep horticultural expertise. Watching the team prepare these beds shows just how much coordination and care it takes to create the spring displays so many New Yorkers look forward to.

What impressed me most is the long-term impact of this process. These bulbs don’t just bloom once and disappear — they’re lifted, replanted, shared, and redistributed so the benefits extend throughout the Park and even into community gardens across the city. It’s a model of sustainability and collaboration that reminds you how much intention sits behind the beauty we enjoy.

The Conservatory Garden is thriving because people show up — staff, volunteers, and community members who believe in keeping this space vibrant all year long. If you’ve ever felt grateful for a moment of calm or color here, know that it’s the result of real hands, real planning, and a real commitment to care.

While in New York for the US Open, I trekked up to 104th Street to see the Conservatory Garden, Central Park’s formal garden. The wisteria wasn’t in bloom and the tulips were long gone, but the garden still felt intentional and quiet in a way that surprises you in New York.

The garden dates back to the 1930s, and you can feel that history the moment you walk through the Vanderbilt Gate. My favourite area was the South Garden, styled as an English perennial garden. The Burnett Fountain sits by the waterlily pool as a tribute to Frances Hodgson Burnett, author of The Secret Garden.

It sits between 104th and 106th on the East Side and it’s a great starting point for a walk down Fifth Avenue toward Museum Mile.

Blondie and Ruth went for a walk in the Conservatory Garden, a cozy corner located in Central Park. It was a quiet sunny day, November was coming to an end and the sky was as high as it gets in the fall. The girls came to the garden by different routes, but they met by the lake and went together to walk Blondie’s poodle and look at the wild geese.
The Conservatory Garden is a formal garden in the northeast corner of New York City’s Central Park. The Conservatory Garden takes its name from the conservatory that stood on the site from 1898 to 1935. Beneath a dogwood-lined staircase, the centerpiece of the Conservatory Garden is a symmetrical lawn outlined in the form of a clipped yew tree, with a single central fountain jet at the rear. It is flanked by two avenues of crabapple trees and rests on a curving wisteria pergola on a steep natural slope.

Блонді та Рут вийшли на прогулянку до Консерваторського саду - затишний куточок що знаходиться в Централ парку. Був тихий сонячний день, листопад добігав кінця і небо було так високо, як буває дише восени. Дівчата прийшли до саду різними шляхами, але зустрілись біля озера і пішли разом вигуляти пуделя Блонді і подивитись на диких гусей.
Консерваторі Гарден – це формальний сад в північно-східному кутку Центрального парку Нью-Йорк. Сад отримав свою назву від консерваторії, що стояла на місці з 1898 по 1935 рік. Під сходами, оточеними кизилом, центральна частина саду це симетричний газон, змальований у вигляді обрізаного тиса, з однієї центральної струменем фонтану ззаду. Він оточений двома алеями крабових яблук і спирається на вигнуту перголу гліцинії на крутому природному схилі.

Jimminy Christmas!!! I’m seriously so blown away with the power of these agentic AI coding tools!
I am not a skilled coder, but I went from nothing to having:
-A homemade remote spectrometer API running via a windows bridge machine
(coded in a day)
-A custom DMX control and color mixing API 
(coded in a second day) 
to now: 
-A fully developed and debugged spectral calibration tool suite (coded in a LONG third day) with slick GUI that integrates the earlier modules to automatically generate flexible fixture profiles with metadata, automatically channel sweeps them and performs spectral measurements (with lots of adjustable measurement setup variables tweakable), develops a library of fixture profiles with customs LUTs, and compiles the measurements into some pretty nifty data structures to prepare them for heavy crunching in the soon-to-be-coded next modules in the stack.

Any one of these modules would be an impressive feat to code. Period. But today’s progress alone would have taken a talented coder 𝚕𝚒𝚝𝚎𝚛𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚢 several WEEKS of coding and hair pulling troubleshooting to implement. At LEAST!!!

The power of these agentic AI coding tools cannot be overstated. Get in there and build the things you’ve always wished existed!

P.S. ClaudeCode running in VS Code for extremely granular planning, prompt refinement, and Primary Build. Gemini in Antigravity for a fresh troubleshooting perspective when Claude gets stuck. It’s a fantastic synergy.

The real reason I don’t use DND is because all my notifications are off by default. Only text messages, nothing else. So in the first portion of the research, the idea that the average Gen Z gets 180+ a day gives a lot of validity to the use. It’s safe to assume that the 180 are not all from loved ones. And that really is one of the most interesting paradoxes with design and technology. The smartphone is designed to turbocharge connection and communication and 10 years later it’s become such a bother, we have to stop all notifications because they distract us from our actual lives. Every design decision comes with second order effects… what do you know!

Also people have 74 unread messages on average on iMessage. We live in such an abundance of stimulation that complete silence is easier than manual selection. 

I also wonder, do people expect a prompt response when the person is not on DND?

❄️🧤 Led by @rutgerssasn Dr. Ramona Ross, students in her “Community Psychology” course put learning into action through a community-centered initiative supported by the Sheila Y. Oliver Center for Politics and Race in America @cprarutgers “Classroom Enrichment Grant.”

Through the grant, Dr. Ross enriched course material by supporting a Newark community initiative focused on assisting individuals who are unsheltered through cold-weather kits. Students collected and packed essential items, including hygiene products and cold-weather supplies. Nearly 100 kits were assembled during class and later distributed through the @rutgers_pd “Winter Blessing Drive,” an annual effort that provides care items to individuals and families across Newark during the colder months.

💌 The grant also supported a second initiative in partnership with the Office of Community & Rutgers Engaged Science (CARES) @rutgers_cares , distributing 56 new hoodies with handwritten notes of encouragement to CASA of Essex County, an advocacy organization supporting youth in foster care.

This initiative reflects the power of purpose-driven learning to make a real difference in Newark and strengthen Rutgers–Newark’s bond with our city.

Chris Peebles is a composer, arranger, jazz musician, and multi-instrumentalist based in New York City. Originally from North Carolina, his work encompasses a wide variety of genres and styles, while remaining firmly rooted in a deep respect for the tradition of Black American music and its many offshoots.

Peebles has composed and arranged music for Broadway productions, television commercials, video games, live orchestras, jazz ensembles, and funk and R&B albums.
Notable credits include working alongside Branford Marsalis and Darrell Waters to orchestrate music for A Wonderful World: The Louis Armstrong Musical, composing works for Jazz at Lincoln Center’s Young Jazz Ensemble publications, and providing arrangements for artists such as Becca Stevens, Camille Thurman, Alexa Tarantino, and Lage Lund, among other notable jazz and contemporary musicians.

Chris also wrote and arranged music for the group Reliably Bad, a North Carolina based band with a wide fan base and millions of streams and views.

The event was held at the iconic @cipriani South Street. I snuck in a bathroom selfie…just cause.😉

I was genuinely delighted and honored to be a selected delegate at the Dubai Business Forum USA yesterday, an incredible event powered by Dubai Chambers and organized by Semafor.

It was a privilege to reconnect with leaders I’ve known for over a decade in the MENA region, and to connect with new, forward-thinking executives committed to global growth.

As the US and Dubai celebrate 50 years of global cooperation, the joint leadership unveiled ambitious plans for the next 50 years, centering on:

Co-leadership in Clean Energy, Space, and AI.

Resilient Supply Chains across continents.

Youth-driven Innovation ecosystems.

Shared global challenges like climate, security, and health (all core to my company’s agenda).

When asked what the key to this future cooperation would be, my answer was simple: It’s a model based on building and sustaining deep trust in people.

H.E. Eng. Sultan Bin Saeed Al Mansoori, Chairman of Dubai Chambers also informed all of us that the inauguration of Dubal International Chamber’s Office will be in New York City. I can feel the near future bilateral trade reach record numbers surpassing the current approximately 32 bn USD (2024 estimates by the Office of the United States Trade Representative).

📸: See you all in the next forum in Dubai, Habibis❣️

#DubaiBusinessForum #GlobalCooperation #Leadership #Innovation #TrustInPeople #Dubai #USMENA

In 1963, the UAE sent its first delegation to the United States, planting the seeds of what has become one of the region’s most dynamic partnerships.

Today I was honored to take part in the inauguration of the first Dubai International Chamber office in New York City — a moment that builds on that 60-year history of cooperation and looks ahead to a new era of innovation and shared growth.

Under Dubai’s D33 Agenda, the vision is clear: to double the size of its economy and become a top three global city within the next decade. The UAE’s commitment to connectivity, investment, and technology continues to inspire all of us building bridges between industries, nations, and ideas.

Excited to see where this next chapter of U.S.–UAE partnership leads 🇺🇸 🇦🇪

Proud teacher moment ✨

I often tell my students: “When you’re a star, shining comes natural.”

Last week, that truth came to life. My students have been shining so brightly — I’m just catching all of their reflections. 🌟

Let me tell y’all why I’m so proud of them:
💄 One student received 10 pre-orders for her homemade lip gloss.
🧃 Another sold out of his juices.
💰 And another secured a $50K investment and internship from a well-known philanthropist.

And while I’m teaching them entrepreneurship, they’re teaching me stewardship. I take pride in continuing to learn, grow, and build a better future for us all — several ideas at a time (LOL).

Because leadership isn’t about perfection or performance — it’s about participation and purpose.

When we empower the future of builders this way — through trust, experimentation, and shared growth — everybody wins: the students, the school, the district, and the movement reminding us that Ownership Is The Future. 💫

“As of yesterday, #ICE is attacking the town of #Huron, California. There are tanks rolling through the streets, and there are armed militia surrounding homes. It’s a state of horror. My opening piece was to contrast against the beauty of the people that are actually being kidnapped and shipped away, broken away from their families, the chaos that we’re seeing right now.”
@willychavarria 

This feeling of #fear #uncertainty #horror was what was running through #Irish/#Mexican American designer @willychavarria’s mind before his first Paris Fashion Week show. The families of Huron, his hometown, his community, were under attack by our own government. 

“My family was under attack from #ICE. I was on the phone with my uncle and aunts, and they were hiding people as #ICE was rounding up people in my hometown.”

Where others have muted themselves, Willy just gets more #heroically vocal, even on the biggest day of his #fashion career thus far. 

Bravo @willychavarria!

…as I unveiled “Aaina” FW 2025 collection for @nyfw X The Silk Road with @pankti_doshi 

Designing this collection or any piece for that matter is more than putting together a beautiful outfit. I know for a fact how fashion can change and transform you for the better. Even though we are super self critical, keeping that internal dialogue healthy and positive is more important than wearing a brand. You have this one life, this one body and it is YOUR responsibility to celebrate it, honor it and flaunt it. We take so much of “what we have now” for granted in the chase of that better waist line, that smoother complexion, that nod of approval from some Aunty sitting far away who has her own trauma to deal with but she has the audacity to tell you “ how you look” and let that affect your judgement of yourself. Ladies! You decide how you want to present yourself and yes we have our clumsy pajama days BUT let’s not forget that we can step on that red carpet and be the  Queen of our own story, any day. Every Single Day. 

Thank you to the women in my life near and far who inspired this collection in so many ways. I am grateful, honored and humbled to be on this journey to find my own answers to what makes me feel beautiful and with that help many other women like me who were once told “ you are not good enough “ as you are. Breaking myths and stereotypes in this ever changing world of Fashion is what supercharges me:)

Brat behavior discourse of the week 

@puptosa is publicly accusing his handler @themazrim of skipping his weekly bath. Odin is away so this is advanced, extra-credit brattiness. (It also reminds me of my pup Ruffus telling everyone I “abandon” him… even if I’m just going to the bathroom.)

What I actually love about this little social media “drama” is that it highlights two things bratty behavior gets right:

1. You don’t get to be this public, playful, and unthreatened unless the dynamic is secure. That level of teasing only works when the relationship underneath it is solid.
2. Good brats understand that you need rules in order to bend them. Brattiness lives inside a framework. You’ve gotta know the rules to break them.

It’s actually a beautiful exchange between people who care deeply for each other.

So am I on Team Tosa (give him a bath) or Team Odin (punish him)? Honestly… both. If it was me, Tosa would absolutely get a bath—but I hope he’s prepared for some very intentional submersion, intense breath work, and learning why brats don’t bite the hand that holds the leash.

This time of year can feel heavy.

Behind the smiles and celebrations, so many of us are carrying things no one sees.
Quiet decisions. Long nights. Risks taken without applause. Wins we didn’t stop to celebrate.

This photo made me think about the “packages” this year brought.
Some showed up as joy and growth.
Others arrived as lessons we didn’t ask for.
All of them asked something of us.

If you’re ending the year tired but still standing… proud but reflective… hopeful even with uncertainty—you’re not behind. You’re human.

My wish for you this season:
that you see the value of what you carried,
the impact of what you built,
and the strength it took to keep going.

Save this for when you need it and don’t forget to share it with someone who’s been holding it together

Wishing you a holiday season that brings you peace, real rest, and incredible moments that feel like a deep breath.

1. Financials & Team (The “In-House” Work)
Trailing 12 (T-12): We’ll review the actual income and expenses month-by-month for the last year or more.

Bank Statement Reconciliation: We’ll match the deposits on the bank statements to the income reported on the T-12. If they don’t match, the income might be “padded”.

Expense Audit: We’ll review 2 years of utility bills (water, electric, gas), property tax bills, and insurance claim history.

Capital Expenditures (CapEx): We’ll review receipts for any major work the seller claims to have done (e.g., “new roof 2023”) to verify warranties and quality.

2. Physical Inspection (The “Boots on the Ground”)

Unit Walkthroughs: Walk 100% of the units. We look for signs of leaks, mold, soft floors, and unauthorized tenants. 

I’LL BE SHARING MY WALK THROUGH CHECKLIST THAT GRADES EACH UNIT AND ALLOWS US TO EASILY IDENTIFY CAP EX COSTS AND PROBLEM UNITS.

Property Condition Assessment (PCA):

Roof & Structure: Foundation cracks, siding issues, and roof life expectancy.

Mechanicals: Age and condition of HVAC units, boilers, and water heaters.

Plumbing: Searching for such things as collapsed pipes under the building using a “sewer scope” to check.

Environmental (Phase I ESA): We’ll ensure there is no soil contamination or underground storage tanks.

3. Lease Audit (The “Tenant” Truth)

Lease Matching: We’ll verify that the rent on the Rent Roll matches the signed leases

4. Legal, Title, and Zoning: We’ll ensure we can actually own and operate the property.

Title Commitment: Our title company will check for liens, unpaid taxes, or easements that “cloud” the title.

Pro Tip: If we find a major issue (like a $50k roof replacement needed), this will be our window to “re-trade”—asking the seller for a price reduction or a credit at closing to cover the repair.

*This is not a solicitation.

Like many auto enthusiasts, I’ve been a fan of the Porsche 911 since I was a kid. Particularly the 993. Whether I was playing Need For Speed High Stakes on my parents’ PC, looking for HotWheels at toy stores, flipping through automotive magazines, or fantasizing about what I’d own/drive some day, I have always gravitated towards this car. 

How fitting, then, that decades later I’d be introduced to the community within @cccmanhattan and handed the keys to the Guards Red 993 C4S you see here. Prior to becoming a club member, I had driven a few 911s up a street or two, but this time was different. I spent an entire day tearing through mountain roads in upstate New York, finally experiencing what makes 911s in general so special during one of the club’s regularly-scheduled member rallies. My skin was buzzing the whole time as I looked down at the Porsche crest on the steering wheel in front of me and took in what was actually happening. I met my childhood hero and it was everything I ever fantasized about as a little boy. 

Naturally, over the next few years, this 993 was the car I took home and drove the most during its time in the club’s fleet. It is also one of many incredible vehicles I’ve been able to experience as intended,  thanks to CCC Manhattan. Join the club and drive. 🏁🏎️💨

New Year Of Life, And Holdin’ On Strong🤘🏼🤠🎂

This year has tested me me in unbelievable ways, as they always do. Some negative experiences definitely included, but lots of positive growth in the end. Hell, even as I’m typing this on the first day of 29 years old- a whole heap of crazy obstacles, hurdles, and unexpected challenges are in full force. The crazy part is that through all of it, I’m genuinely proud to say that my faith hasn’t wavered one bit and I’m still truckin along as always! 🙏🏻

 I’m just so insanely grateful for all of my Family, Friends, and every learning experience that surrounds me every single day. It’s amazing how even in the craziest of times and frustrating moments, quality aspects of life like those really overshadow any sort of madness. I’m going into the new year of life more motivated, resilient, and full of faith than I ever have before- and for that, I’m beyond blessed and insanely grateful. Here’s to all of my new adventures, friendships, and chapters of life in this past year- and also to this next round too, because I can’t wait to see what the Good Lord has in store for me next!🍻

caption:
Gatekeepers
From the birth of humanity to the present, people have sought protection and security. In the past, religion provided comfort and meaning, but in today’s high-tech world, reliance has shifted toward technology.
I created a series called Prophecy of a New Mythology, where I reinterpret traditional religious symbols by integrating technological elements, reflecting the rise of new ”gods“ in the modern era. Gatekeepers is one of the signature works in this series.
Gatekeeper paintings are a form of traditional Chinese folk art, commonly displayed on doors during Chinese New Year’s Eve. These guardian figures, armed with weapons and riding fierce beasts, are believed to offer protection. In my reinterpretation, I modernize the concept of gatekeepers by depicting today’s protectors—police officers and firefighters—while preserving the essence of traditional gatekeeper paintings.
